title: Chapter 22: Beyond Words
content:
Chapter 22:

Inexpressible Words

”————————!!”

He cannot perceive the moment his consciousness returned.

A ringing in his ears like torrential rain falling right beside him; his vision flickers alternately between red and white, and the world is tilted distortedly, unpleasantly.

Sensation does not transmit to his limbs, and his throat is straining with a scream thick beyond thought at the agony of his entrails being wrung out.

He twists his body which will not obey him, making it bounce, using every movable part of his whole body to convert the incomprehensible passion welling up within his chest into destruction.

He doesn’t know what is what.

Where did the pain vanish to? Why is his consciousness not clear? Where are the wounds that were ravaging his whole body? Blood is draining away, life is draining away, he is dying.

I don’t want to die. I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die.

Pain and hardship and suffering and sadness and fear, he hates it all.

He wants to push it all away, yet those are the only things he can find within reach. So, surrendering to impulse, he tries to protect his own heart by striking, crushing, tearing, throwing away, and discarding those negative emotions at random.

“————————!”

He can hear something. He can hear someone’s voice.

Mixed into the beast-like roars, he can hear the voice of someone clinging to him desperately.

The meaning doesn’t get through. He doesn’t understand the meaning. He doesn’t want to understand the meaning.

It’s useless even if he listens. Listening will only hurt him. It’s not as if listening will change anything. Nothing will change even if he listens.

Even so, gradually, gradually, the colors of the world become clear.

Blood circulates to the tips of his limbs, and the sensation of his thrashing body is transmitted correctly to his nerves.

His arms, having rampaged and rampaged, seem to have struck something hard repeatedly; his nails are broken, his knuckles split, and they seem to be bleeding terribly.

Sharp pain stabs his brain, and his wailing slows its momentum ever so slightly.

And then he notices. That something warm is clinging to his aching arm, around the right upper arm, as if wrapping it up.

There was a similar sensation on his legs. Something small is covering his legs, which he had raised to strike the floor over and over again, from directly above, sealing their movement.

Color returns to his vision. Spreading out before his eyes is a white ceiling he remembers seeing several times.

From the circulation of his blood and the weight on his back, he realizes he is lying face up. The soft sensation belongs to a bed; he had been sleeping with his limbs thrown out.

And, the ones who had physically restrained his thrashing limbs in that posture were,

“Guest, Guest. Have you calmed down yet?”

“Guest, Guest. Are you done going completely mad?”

The moment those two familiar voices struck his eardrums, Subaru’s brain stopped thinking and selected only one thing: a scream.

※※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

For Subaru, the morning of his first day at the Roswaal manor, totaling the fourth time, opened its curtains in the worst form yet.

Subaru has already lost his life six times in this world and returned.

None of the ways he died were ever easy, and each time, he has tasted the agony of having what he gained spill from his hands once more.

He never gets used to the pain or the suffering, and the sense of desolation and loss that arises every time he returns is not something anyone can share with him.

Even so, Subaru intends to have lived looking forward earnestly, simply clenching his teeth. He has resolved that he would not bend his knees, that he would not lose in spirit alone.

However, this instance cannot be compared to anything before.

The sense of loss, the sense of desolation, the pain, the suffering—all of it gouged deeply and sharply into Subaru’s heart, proportional to the bonds of the days spent until now.

There is no way he can stand. The will to stand does not even well up. He cannot even think of a reason why he must stand. It is that kind of situation.

“—Okay, all done. The wound should be closed, but you mustn’t be too rough. If it happens to bleed again, just call me.”

Gently stroking the back of Subaru’s right hand, the girl sitting in the chair next to the bed smiles at him.

Tying her silver hair into a single bundle, wearing faint blue light on her palm, is Emilia.

She had rushed over and was healing Subaru with healing magic after he suffered lacerations on his hands from thrashing about immediately after waking up.

The only ones in the room are Subaru and Emilia.

The other two who happened to be there the moment he woke up had bowed their heads and disappeared, never to return, upon seeing Subaru’s unsightly behavior right after he noticed them.

“I heard from Ram and Rem, that… you said some terrible things to the two of them?”

At the mention of names he didn’t want to hear, Subaru lifted his face as if flicked.

Emilia opened her eyes slightly at that excessive reaction, but upon recognizing the expression of agitation running across Subaru’s face, she pursed her lips,

“They were unusually down, thinking they might have done something rude. So next time you see them, please say something to them.”

“Something rude, huh. No, there was noth—ing. …Between me and those two, there was noth—ing at all.”

His somewhat throwaway voice was hoarse, and Emilia’s well-shaped brows furrowed softly at the aftereffect of the ill feeling contained within it.

Even seeing that, no apology or comfort comes from Subaru’s mouth.

What slipped out instead was a question that couldn’t quite be called sarcasm.

“Hey, Emilia-tan… don’t you think I’m a nuisance?”

“Tan… you really…”

Emilia shows a rejection-like reaction to the address for a split second as usual, but Subaru’s attitude in asking the question does not lose its seriousness for a moment.

She contemplated silently for a while, prefaced with “Not really,” and held up a finger,

“There’s no way I’d think you’re a nuisance. Besides, Subaru is my lifesaver, right? If my lifesaver disappeared on his own without me repaying that debt, I’d sleep poorly. So, for the sake of my pride, I’d be troubled if you disappeared before I repay the debt.”

Speaking fast, Emilia asserts this as if to gloss over some kind of emotion.

Listening to it intently, Subaru watched her every move. Was there any falsehood there? Did it contain any reactions or gestures hiding something?

“Oi oi, seriously…”

Realizing that he was gauging her reaction with eyes of suspicion, Subaru muttered the sound aloud, unable to hide his discouragement and disappointment in himself.

Unexpectedly, hadn’t Emilia just said it? If he can no longer even think of his lifesaver as such, then that is truly the lowest behavior.

Emilia was supposed to be the only oasis where Subaru could entrust his heart in this other world where he had no one to rely on.

The possibilities that he should have been able to think of in the same way, even if not to her extent, have now disappeared from before Subaru in a merciless form.

If he loses even his absolute trust in her at this point, that would be nothing other than Subaru walking through pitch darkness by touch alone.

Suddenly, a thought crossed his mind.

If only he could confess the despair occupying this chest, and the situation he has tried to redo and challenge over and over again, to her and no one else.

Thinking back, Subaru has continued to struggle to manage all the mortal crises that have visited him time and time again with his own hands alone.

But the situation has reached extreme destitution, and it has already come to a point where neither advancing nor retreating allows Subaru any easy choices.

In that case, wouldn’t confiding the matter to a third party—a trustworthy person—and begging for assistance be the brilliant move to play to reach the best outcome?

As if fog were clearing, the emotions of anxiety and bewilderment that had been hanging over Subaru’s head were blown away.

Once he realized it, it was such a naturally acceptable method that he didn’t know why he had removed that option from his candidates until now.

“—Emilia-tan, there is something I want you to hear.”

Lowering the tone of his voice, Subaru turns to face Emilia.

She must have sensed the change in atmosphere. Emilia, too, floated tension on her sorrowful face, corrected her posture on the chair, and looked at him from directly in front.

Watching his reflection in her violet-blue eyes, Subaru slowly begins by choosing the first word.

What should he speak of? About “Return by Death”? Or should he speak nakedly from the point that Subaru is not an existence of this world in the first place?

It is a story likely to be laughed off, and the probability of it being taken as a joke is far higher. Even so, surely she alone would not treat Subaru’s serious plea casually.

That expectation, that hope, was everything supporting Subaru right now.

—I will speak about “Return by Death.” And, if possible, I want you to lend me your strength.

While feeling ashamed of his own wretchedness in seeking it again from someone he had received a debt from, Subaru swallows his breath and forms the first voice. From there, the situation will begin to move.

Extremely confused, forced to throw in the towel saying it’s helpless. The light to the situation he had almost given up on opens from there.

—That, is what he thought.

“————”

The moment he thought to put it into words, to form his voice, it visited.

A sense of wrongness; receiving it, Subaru hesitates on the first word in bewilderment.

Thinking something is wrong, he immediately realized the reason. Sound. Sound had vanished. From the world, suddenly, sound had disappeared. The sound of his own heart beating fast, which he could hear just moments ago. The faint breathing of Emilia in front of him. The quiet coloring of the morning breeze sneaking in through the slightly open window and circulating in the room.

All of it had vanished completely from the world.

A world without sound—it is an isolated space where even the word “silence” is lukewarm. An absolute state of silence, no questions asked, where even the sound of ringing ears is erased, where even the sound of blood flowing through the body cannot be heard.

Just by having that done to him, chills run through his whole body, and an unbearable discomfort rampages as if stirring up his entrails.

And that was merely the beginning of the anomaly.

—What, is this

?

From the world where sound had vanished, next, the movement of all existence vanished.

Time is stretched out, an instant becomes eternity, and one second later changes its arrival point greatly to the distant yonder of time.

Before his eyes, Emilia’s expression does not move from her serious look. Her eyelids do not twitch, and her lips remain tightly sealed.

Remaining in her dignified appearance, Emilia is distanced from her next movement eternally. And that is the same for Subaru; the length of his thoughts that he was supposed to voice will likely never be delivered to anyone if things stay this way.

Sound vanishes, time stops, and Subaru’s earnest wish is distanced.

A phenomenon beyond understanding that arrived suddenly. His body, through which nerves do not pass, cannot be moved a fragment, and Subaru simply continues to race his thoughts while holding onto his confusion.

Incomprehensible. Incomprehensible. Incomprehensible. Incomprehensible. Incomprehensible—

What is the reason for this? He doesn’t even have the mental leeway to guess.

Simply, in the domain of non-understanding that comes in waves, Subaru can do nothing but continue to scream his lamentation inside his brain as if overwhelmed.

And, the end of that sensation revealed its form abruptly.

—What is this?

A voice of doubt floats in his mind, and Subaru tilts his head in image only.

Ahead of his gaze, within the fixed, unmoving field of vision, he could only think that it had arisen suddenly.

It is a black haze. For Subaru, who didn’t even have the freedom to blink, its appearance could only be described as abrupt in the truest sense.

Cutting into his consciousness, It was drifting in that spot.

What was even more singular, however, was that only that black haze slowly changed its shape.

In a world where everything has stagnated, only the black haze changes shape at a gentle speed. A haze of a mass about enough to be held in both hands makes its outline clearer little by little, and finally reaches its target shape taking over ten seconds in perceived time.

—To Subaru, it looked like a black palm.

The haze that changed shape had taken the form of an arm.

A floating black arm possessing five fingers and only length up to the elbow.

And It trembled its fingertips as if checking, then closed in on Subaru with clear intent.

Watching it helplessly, Subaru swallowed his breath in sensation alone.

The black fingertips sneak into Subaru’s chest smoothly, as if there were nothing to obstruct them. And, the sensation of those fingertips clearly caressing his internal organs was transmitted to Subaru.

Touching his entrails, stroking his ribs, the palm proceeds further in, and eventually delivers its fingertips to the most important organ in the human body.

—Oi, wait.

A voice that does not become a voice. A body that cannot resist. Without being able to make a single movement, not understanding the black palm’s motive or anything else, fear races through Subaru’s whole body.

—This is seriously, not fu—

Before he could finish saying it in his heart, a shock shook Subaru’s existence from the foundation.

Is there a human alive who can explain why it hurts to have one’s internal organs damaged? The answer to that is simple; it can be summed up in one phrase: there is no need to think about such a thing.

In that instant, the intense pain that assaulted Subaru did not have a fragment of necessity for reasoning.

Just simply, earnestly, the pain of having his heart crushed without mercy continued to batter Subaru.

He cannot raise his voice. He is forbidden even from trembling in pain.

With no means to gloss over the pain, who other than Subaru in this moment could understand the pain of feeling nothing but pain?

Only agony was there. And bringing along something that was not just agony, it left a warning for Subaru that was grateful enough to bring tears to his eyes.

The existence known as Subaru was torn apart by the pain, his consciousness distorted as if treated roughly, his thoughts shredded to ribbons so badly he couldn’t remember their original shape—

“—Subaru?”

“—Huh?”

“Subaru, are you okay? You went silent suddenly, you’re making me worry.”

Placing a hand on his knee, a silver beauty was staring at Subaru with eyes harboring sorrow.

The moment he became conscious of that, Subaru leaked a long breath as if deflating. Then he confirmed that his fingers moved according to his will, and touching his own chest with a delay, he confirmed from the outside that his heart was carving out a quiet rhythm.

His body moves. His voice comes out. He feels no pain in his heart.

But, the fear was carved into him.

His fingertips tremble, his voice refuses to come out, and his body remains shrunken and frozen.

Proportional to the hope that had arisen, the fact brought about by It made Subaru despair.

Just thinking in a corner of his head that he would muster his courage and challenge It again, the illusion of a black haze crossing the edge of Subaru’s vision floats up.

And, Subaru is finally forced to admit it.

To Subaru who covers his face with his palms as if yielding to the welling despair, shrinking atop the bed, Emilia floats bewilderment and opens her mouth,

“W-What’s wrong? You’ve been really strange for a while now, you know? If there is something…”

“—I have a request.”

Interrupting the voice concerned for him, Subaru turns his palm toward her.

He cannot lift his face. Surely, he is making a terrible face. If he looks at her in this mental state, he cannot trust himself regarding what he might blurt out.

Mobilizing all his self-control, Subaru creates just a single phrase.

Discarding the words he intended to say, the feelings he wanted her to hear, the passion he truly wished to confess from the bottom of his heart—everything.

“Emilia-tan.”

“Y-Yeah. Tell me anything.”

“Don’t concern yourself with me.”

Conveying only that feebly, he collapses onto the bed without looking at her reaction.

Unconsciously his palm touches his chest, and while feeling the beat beneath it through his thin skin, Subaru clearly realizes the reality that has been thrust upon him.

—Confessing is not forgiven.

—That Subaru has no choice but to continue struggling alone.
